title: Emberfield throughput & p95 readiness call
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private decision factors
summary: Initial discovery to map Emberfield's latency & throughput targets for a conversational agent. Customer is evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private; main concerns are p95 <= 250ms for short replies, token/sec sustained throughput during peak surges, and data residency/KS encryption. Agreed to run a focused token/sec + streaming p95 benchmark and share security docs.
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark harness + sample config and cost estimate (Maya)
Customer to provide representative prompt set and traffic curve CSV (Priya)
Schedule 1-hour benchmark kickoff next week (Liam/Maya + Priya/Diego)
Redwood to attach SOC 2 + SSO/KMS docs to CRM (Maya)
Customer to validate legal constraints for VPC/on-prem within EU region (Asha)

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2029-01-15 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Brooks (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (CTO, Emberfield), Diego Ramos (Head of Platform), Priya Nair (ML Infra), Samir (PM)

Auto-summary (auto): discuss p95 targets, streaming token throughput, choose hosting mode, run benchmarks

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about 45 minutes, quick intros?
00:12 Asha Patel: hi, Asha here, CTO at Emberfield, we run the agent product for customer support and a few internal automation things.
00:21 Diego Ramos: Diego, platform, we manage k8s clusters, currently on a mixed cloud footprint.
00:28 Priya Nair: Priya, infra for ML, I own model infra and perf testing.
00:33 Maya Chen: great, Liam will run the technical bits.
00:36 Liam Brooks: hi all, quick agenda, understand current targets (p95), traffic patterns, streaming vs non-streaming, and security constraints, then propose a benchmark plan. sound ok?
00:50 Asha Patel: yes, goal is to get a sense if Redwood Hosted can meet our p95 SLAs or if we need Dedicated or Private, especially for EU customers.
01:02 Diego Ramos: to add, pricing is important but reliability and data controls are top.

01:15 Liam Brooks: can you share your p95 numbers? what have you been seeing?
01:22 Priya Nair: currently in our staging we see p95 around 420-480ms for 256-token turns using our open model stack, that's with small batching. Production is variable—during peaks CPU and GPU contention pushes it higher. Our target is p95 <= 250ms for short replies (< 128 tokens), and for longer streaming responses we want 95th streaming latency under 350ms for initial token and sustainable token/sec at 80–120 tokens/sec per session.
01:52 Maya Chen: that's helpful. when you say streaming initial token 350ms, is that from request to first token or token emission interval?
01:59 Priya Nair: first token emission, and steady state throughput measured as tokens/sec per active session. during campaigns we've seen bursts of 8–12k concurrent sessions.
02:13 Diego Ramos: concurrency wise, typical steady is ~700 sessions, peak can spik– spike to 10k over an hour during promo windows.
02:23 Maya Chen: ok, big swings. are sessions mostly short chat or multi-turn with memory?
02:30 Samir: mostly short, but some flows do 5–8 turns with KV cache used.

02:40 Liam Brooks: good, so for sizing we need token/sec distribution, seq len distribution, and concurrency curves—Priya can you share that?
02:49 Priya Nair: yes, we'll share a 7-day CSV with per-minute RPS and average tokens per session, also a prompt corpus.
03:00 Maya Chen: perfect. high-level tradeoffs: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value, we run optimized kernels and prefix/KV caching for performance—these typically reduce cost and p95. Dedicated gives reserved capacity if you want predictable SLOs and throughput. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict data residency and egress control.
03:22 Asha Patel: our legal/compliance team is pushing for EU residency for EU customers; we'd prefer a VPC or private control plane. what's the difference in latency between Hosted EU region and Dedicated in our tenancy?
03:36 Liam Brooks: Hosted in EU region is colocated; p95 delta is usually within 10–20% depending on model and seq len. Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs so variance is small and tail latencies are better under noisy neighbor scenarios. For p95 <= 250ms short replies, Dedicated or small private pool is often the safer path if you have sustained concurrency.
04:00 Diego Ramos: what about autoscaling? we have big spikes, want to avoid cold start issues.
04:06 Liam Brooks: Redwood Dedicated supports fast burst capacity plus warm pools; cold starts are minimized via pre-warming and we can pin model versions. For Hosted, we have autoscaling and a fallback to smaller variants, but there is a brief window where p95 may increase during ramp. We can test burst behavior in the benchmark.
04:27 Priya Nair: curious about caching—KV cache and prefix caching—how much improvement do you typically see?
04:33 Maya Chen: it really depends on prompt repetition. For high reuse it's up to 40% token cost reduction and noticeable p95 wins because fewer tokens are recomputed; for conversational contexts with unique prompts it's less effective.
04:47 Liam Brooks: also continuous batching helps throughput; we tune batch windows to balance latency vs throughput. we usually start conservative for p95-focused benchmarks.

05:00 Asha Patel: security notes: we need SOC 2, SSO (SAML), audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and KMS integration for key control. Any limitations?
05:12 Maya Chen: Redwood has SOC 2 reports; SAML SSO, RBAC and audit logs are supported. For KMS, Dedicated and Private allow customer-managed keys and HSM options. We'll drop the security pack in the CRM.
05:24 Diego Ramos: EU KMS residency?
05:28 Liam Brooks: yes, with Private deployment we can keep keys and control plane within your VPC—no egress. For Hosted, we support region-specific storage but you should review DPA specifics.

05:42 Samir: on the benchmark, what do you need from us?
05:46 Liam Brooks: ideally sample prompts, seq len distribution, tokens per second expectation, concurrency curve, and whether streaming is used. We'll run token/sec sustained tests and streaming p95 tests. We'll share a harness repo and quickstart.
05:58 Maya Chen: link we'll send: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/emberfield (note: placeholder link) and a spreadsheet template for traffic curve.
06:12 Priya Nair: good. what hardware do you use in Dedicated?
06:15 Liam Brooks: our Dedicated pools are typically A100-class and similar NV-series in partner clouds; we also support some quantized CPU paths for embed-only workloads. For streaming and p95 tight targets, GPU-backed runtimes are recommended.
06:30 Diego Ramos: quantization tradeoffs? we saw some quality drift on 4-bit for our model family.
06:36 Liam Brooks: yes, quantization can save cost but may impact output quality. Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per workload; we'll include initial suggested profiles but recommend validation by your eval set.

06:50 Asha Patel: any rough numbers—tokens/sec per GPU and expected p95 for short replies?
06:55 Liam Brooks: ballpark, depends heavily on model size. For a 7B-ish model optimized on our runtime, a single A100 can do sustained ~10k–20k tokens/sec for simple generation; p95 for 64–128 token replies often sits in the 80–200ms range under load if batching is tuned. Larger models will reduce that. We'll capture specifics in the benchmark output.
07:21 Priya Nair: can you simulate multi-region failover? we need to know cross-region latency impact.
07:27 Liam Brooks: yes, we can run a multi-region stress test; smart routing will fallback to other regions and we can show delta. If you require strict EU residency, failover needs to be scoped to EU-only nodes.
07:41 Maya Chen: are there any legal blockers you've seen for Private deployments?
07:45 Asha Patel: nothing yet, our procurement will vet costs, but security is the big gating factor.

08:00 Speaker 6 (unknown): sorry late, joined. question—how do you handle model rollouts and regressions?
08:07 Liam Brooks: good Q. We support canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback if quality regressions are detected against pre-defined eval prompts. We can hook your eval sets into Redwood Optimize for alerting.
08:20 Priya Nair: that would be great. we have a 500-prompt gold set.
08:24 Maya Chen: share that with us and we'll integrate into the pilot.

08:33 Diego Ramos: cost concerns—if we pick Dedicated what's the commit cadence? monthly? annual?
08:40 Maya Chen: Dedicated is typically reserved capacity with monthly or annual contracts; there are burst credits for short windows. We can produce a cost estimate in the follow-up.
08:50 Asha Patel: what's the expected timeline to run the benchmark and get results?
08:53 Liam Brooks: once we get prompts and traffic CSV, we can run an initial pass in 2–3 business days; full tuning and a second pass for dedicated sizing might take 7–10 days.
09:05 Maya Chen: ok, let's recap next steps—Maya will send harness + security docs, Priya will upload prompt set and traffic curve, Liam will propose dedicated sizing, and we schedule benchmark kickoff.
09:20 Asha Patel: yes, thanks. Diego and I will review and loop in procurement after results.
09:28 Maya Chen: perfect, thank you everyone. we'll follow up with links and a calendar invite for the kickoff.
09:34 End of call

Notes: occasional mis-transcripts observed (numbers sometimes fuzzy), speakers overlapped around 08:00; link references are placeholders.
